ja: 宇宙全体を満たす「宇宙マイクロ波背景放射」の温度は約−270℃。絶対零度よりわずか2.7度高いだけ。
easy: The light left over from the start of the universe is very cold, only 2.7 degrees above the coldest possible temperature.
std: The cosmic microwave background, the afterglow of the Big Bang, has a temperature of just 2.7 degrees above absolute zero, about minus 270°C.

ja: 地球の中心（内核）の温度は約5200℃で、太陽の表面とほぼ同じくらい熱い。
easy: The center of the Earth is about as hot as the surface of the sun.
std: Earth's inner core is about 5,200°C, roughly as hot as the surface of the Sun.

ja: 宇宙にある原子の約9割は水素、残りのほとんどはヘリウム。そのほかの元素をすべて合わせても1%ほどしかない。
easy: Most atoms in space are hydrogen. Almost all the rest are helium.
std: About 90% of the atoms in the universe are hydrogen and most of the rest are helium; all other elements together make up only around 1%.

ja: ウイルスが生き物かどうかは今も議論がある。自分だけでは増えられず、他の生き物の細胞を使って増えるため。
easy: Scientists still argue about whether viruses are alive. They can only make copies of themselves inside other living cells.
std: Whether viruses count as living things is still debated, because they can reproduce only inside the cells of another organism.

ja: ブラックホールの中心（特異点）では、今の物理学の法則がうまく当てはまらなくなる。
easy: At the center of a black hole, our rules of science stop working.
std: At the singularity at the heart of a black hole, our current laws of physics, including general relativity, break down.

ja: 周期表の118の元素のうち、自然界で見つかるのは約94。残りは研究所で人工的に作られた。
easy: There are 118 known elements. About 94 are found in nature, and people made the rest in labs.
std: Of the 118 known chemical elements, about 94 occur naturally; the rest have only been made in laboratories.

ja: 地球で見つかった最も古い鉱物の粒は約44億年前のもの。月の石には約45億年前のものもある。
easy: The oldest small piece of rock found on Earth is about 4.4 billion years old.
std: The oldest known mineral grains on Earth, zircons from Australia, are about 4.4 billion years old, and some Moon rocks are even older.

ja: 空気は私たちの体をいつも強い力で押している。大人の体全体で約15トン分の力になるが、体の中からも同じ力で押し返しているので感じない。
easy: The air is always pushing on your body very hard. You do not feel it, because your body pushes back just as hard.
std: Air pressure pushes on an adult's body with a total force of around 15 tonnes, but we don't feel it because the pressure inside the body balances it.

ja: さなぎの中で体がほとんど作り直されても、幼虫のときに覚えたことがチョウ（ガ）になっても残っていたという研究がある。
easy: A study found that some insects remember things they learned as young insects, even after they change their whole body.
std: A 2008 study found that moths could remember what they had learned as caterpillars, even after metamorphosis rebuilt their bodies.

ja: ハヤブサは急降下するとき時速380kmを超え、地球上で最も速い動物とされる。
easy: A peregrine falcon can fly down at more than 380 km an hour. It is the fastest animal on Earth.
std: The peregrine falcon can exceed 380 km per hour in a hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

ja: ゾウは足の裏で地面を伝わる低い振動を感じ取り、遠くにいる仲間の声に気づくことができると考えられている。
easy: Elephants may 'hear' with their feet. They can feel very low sounds from other elephants through the ground.
std: Elephants can detect low-frequency rumbles from distant herd members through the ground, sensing the vibrations with their feet.

ja: 木の体のほとんどは、土からではなく空気中の二酸化炭素と水から作られている。
easy: A tree is not made mostly from soil. It is made mostly from air and water.
std: Most of a tree's mass comes not from the soil but from carbon dioxide in the air and water, combined through photosynthesis.

ja: イルカは脳の半分ずつ眠り、もう半分で泳ぎや呼吸を続ける。グンカンドリのように飛びながら眠る鳥もいる。
easy: Dolphins sleep with half of their brain at a time. The other half keeps them swimming and breathing.
std: Dolphins sleep with one half of the brain at a time, so they can keep swimming and breathing; some birds, like frigatebirds, sleep this way in flight.

ja: コウイカは色を見分けられないと考えられているのに、周りの色にそっくり合わせて姿を隠せる。そのしくみはまだよく分かっていない。
easy: Cuttlefish probably cannot see colors, but they can change their color to match what is around them.
std: Cuttlefish are thought to be colorblind, yet they blend into their surroundings with remarkable accuracy, and scientists are still working out how.

ja: アリは1匹ずつは簡単なルールで動くだけなのに、群れ全体では複雑で賢い行動ができる。この考え方はロボットやAIの研究にも使われる。
easy: Each ant follows simple rules, but together, ants can do very smart things. People use this idea in computer science.
std: Individual ants follow simple rules, yet colonies solve complex problems together, an example of swarm intelligence that inspires computer algorithms.

ja: 植物は虫に食べられると、においの成分を出して、近くの植物に危険を知らせることがある。
easy: When insects eat a plant, it can send out a smell that warns other plants nearby.
std: When attacked by insects, some plants release airborne chemicals that can prompt neighboring plants to prepare their defenses.

ja: サンゴは動物で、体の中に小さな藻がすんでいる。藻が光合成で栄養を分け、水温が上がって藻が出ていくとサンゴは白くなる（白化）。
easy: Coral is an animal. Tiny plants live inside it and give it food. When the sea gets too warm, they leave and the coral turns white.
std: Corals are animals that host tiny algae in their tissues; when the water gets too warm the algae leave, and the coral turns white, which is called bleaching.

ja: イエローストーン国立公園にオオカミが戻ったことで、シカの行動が変わり、川辺の植物が回復したといわれる。ただし影響の大きさには議論もある。
easy: When wolves came back to a national park in the US, the deer changed how they lived. This helped plants by the rivers grow again.
std: After wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone, changes in elk behavior are said to have helped riverside plants recover, though scientists debate how large the effect was.

ja: 古代ローマのコロッセオは西暦80年に完成し、5万人以上の観客が入れたと考えられている。
easy: The Colosseum in Rome was finished in the year 80. More than 50,000 people could watch shows there.
std: Completed in AD 80, the Colosseum in Rome could hold an estimated 50,000 or more spectators.

ja: 火薬・羅針盤・紙・印刷術は「中国の四大発明」と呼ばれる。火薬は9世紀ごろの唐の時代に生まれ、10世紀には戦いに使われ始めた。
easy: China gave the world four great inventions: gunpowder, the compass, paper and printing.
std: Gunpowder, the compass, papermaking and printing are known as the Four Great Inventions of China; gunpowder was discovered around the 9th century.

ja: コロンブスはアジアに着いたと信じたまま亡くなったといわれる。アメリカ大陸の名前は、別の探検家アメリゴ・ヴェスプッチから来ている。
easy: Columbus may have died thinking he had reached Asia. America was named after a different explorer, Amerigo Vespucci.
std: Columbus is thought to have believed until his death that he had reached Asia; the Americas were named after another explorer, Amerigo Vespucci.

ja: ガリレオは地動説を支持したため1633年に有罪とされた。カトリック教会が誤りを公式に認めたのは1992年だった。
easy: In 1633, Galileo was found guilty for saying the Earth goes around the sun. The church said it was wrong only in 1992.
std: Galileo was convicted in 1633 for supporting the idea that Earth orbits the Sun; the Catholic Church formally acknowledged its error in 1992.

ja: ギロチンの名前のもとになったギヨタン医師は、死刑そのものに反対していた。のちに家族は名字を変えたといわれる。
easy: Dr. Guillotin, whose name was given to the guillotine, was against killing people as a punishment. Later, his family changed their name.
std: Dr. Joseph-Ignace Guillotin, after whom the guillotine was named, actually opposed the death penalty; his family later changed their surname.

ja: マチュピチュはスペインの征服者に見つからなかった。1911年にハイラム・ビンガムが紹介して世界に知られたが、地元の人々は前から知っていた。
easy: The Spanish never found Machu Picchu. It became famous in 1911, but local people already knew about it.
std: Spanish conquerors never found Machu Picchu; it became world-famous after Hiram Bingham's visit in 1911, though local farmers had long known it.

ja: バイキングには乱暴なイメージがあるが、アイスランドでは930年に「アルシング」という議会を開き、話し合いで物事を決めていた。
easy: Vikings had meetings to make laws. Iceland started one of the oldest such meetings in the year 930.
std: Though remembered as raiders, Norse settlers founded Iceland's Althing in 930, one of the oldest parliaments in the world.

ja: 1884〜85年のベルリン会議などをきっかけに、ヨーロッパの国々はアフリカを分け合い、多くのまっすぐな国境線が引かれた。
easy: In the 1880s, countries in Europe divided Africa among themselves and drew many straight borders.
std: Following the Berlin Conference of 1884-85, European powers divided Africa among themselves, drawing many borders with little regard for local peoples.

ja: ライト兄弟の初飛行（1903年）から、アポロ11号の月面着陸（1969年）まで、わずか66年しかたっていない。
easy: Only 66 years passed between the first plane flight and the first walk on the moon.
std: Just 66 years separate the Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 and the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969.

ja: ぼんやりしているときも脳は休んでいない。「デフォルト・モード・ネットワーク」という脳の部分がむしろ活発に働いている。
easy: Your brain is busy even when you are doing nothing. Some parts work more when you are resting.
std: Even when we are idle, the brain stays busy: a set of regions called the default mode network becomes more active when we daydream.

ja: 心臓は1日に7000リットル以上の血液を送り出している。
easy: Your heart moves more than 7,000 liters of blood every day.
std: The heart pumps more than 7,000 liters of blood around the body every day.

ja: 肺の中の小さな袋（肺胞）は数億個あり、広げると約50〜75m²にもなる。
easy: Your lungs have hundreds of millions of tiny air bags. Spread out, they would cover a big room.
std: The lungs contain hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli, with a total surface area of about 50 to 75 square meters.

ja: 人のゲノム（全遺伝情報）は約30億の文字（塩基対）でできている。
easy: Your genes are written with about three billion 'letters'.
std: The human genome is made up of about three billion base pairs, the 'letters' of DNA.

ja: レム睡眠のとき、脳は起きているときのように活発だが、体の筋肉は力が抜けて動かない。目だけがすばやく動く。
easy: In one stage of sleep, your brain is very busy, but your body cannot move. Only your eyes move fast.
std: During REM sleep the brain is almost as active as when awake, while most muscles are relaxed and still, except for rapid eye movements.

ja: 人の目は約100万色以上を見分けられるとされる。男性の約8%、女性の約0.5%は、特定の色の区別がつきにくい色覚の特徴をもつ。
easy: People can see about a million colors. But about 8% of men find it hard to tell some colors apart.
std: The human eye can distinguish roughly a million colors, but about 8% of men and 0.5% of women have some form of color vision deficiency.

ja: 腸と脳は神経やホルモンでつながっていて、腸内細菌が気分や行動に影響する可能性が研究されている。
easy: Your stomach and your brain talk to each other. Scientists think the small living things in your stomach may change your mood.
std: The gut and brain are linked by nerves and hormones, and researchers are studying how gut bacteria may influence mood and behavior.

ja: 天然痘は、人類が根絶できた唯一の人の感染症（1980年にWHOが宣言）。予防接種のもとを作ったのはジェンナー。
easy: Smallpox is the only human illness people have removed from the world. This was announced in 1980.
std: Smallpox is the only human infectious disease ever eradicated, declared by the WHO in 1980, following vaccination methods pioneered by Edward Jenner.

ja: ピザはイタリア移民によってアメリカに広まり、ニューヨーク風やシカゴ風など、土地ごとに独自のスタイルが生まれた。
easy: Italian people brought pizza to the US. Now cities like New York and Chicago have their own kinds of pizza.
std: Italian immigrants brought pizza to the United States, where regional styles such as New York and Chicago deep-dish developed.

ja: とうがらしの辛さは味ではなく痛みとして感じている。鳥はこの辛さを感じないので、種を遠くまで運んでくれる。
easy: The hot taste of chili is really a feeling of pain. Birds do not feel it, so they eat the seeds and carry them far away.
std: Chili heat is sensed as pain, not taste. Birds can't feel capsaicin, so they eat the peppers and spread the seeds.

ja: オリーブオイルは数千年前から地中海で使われてきた。古代ギリシャの詩人ホメロスは「液体の黄金」と呼んだ。
easy: People around the Mediterranean Sea have used olive oil for thousands of years. A Greek poet called it 'liquid gold'.
std: Olive oil has been used around the Mediterranean for thousands of years; the poet Homer called it 'liquid gold'.

ja: ラーメンは中国の麺料理をもとに日本で独自に発展した。1958年には日清食品が世界初のインスタントラーメンを発売した。
easy: Ramen came from Chinese noodles and changed in Japan. The first instant ramen was sold in 1958.
std: Ramen developed in Japan from Chinese noodle dishes, and in 1958 Nissin released the world's first instant ramen.

ja: チーズは世界に1000種類以上あり、フランスだけでも数百種類がある。
easy: There are more than 1,000 kinds of cheese in the world. France alone has hundreds.
std: There are well over a thousand varieties of cheese worldwide, and France alone produces several hundred.

ja: 緑茶・烏龍茶・紅茶は、すべて同じチャノキの葉から作られる。違いは葉をどれだけ酸化（発酵）させるか。
easy: Green tea, oolong tea and black tea all come from the same plant. They are made in different ways.
std: Green, oolong and black tea all come from the same plant, Camellia sinensis; the difference lies in how much the leaves are oxidized.

ja: バニラはサフランに次いで高価なスパイス。花を手で受粉させる必要があり、世界の生産の多くをマダガスカルが占める。
easy: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice. Each flower must be helped by hand to make fruit.
std: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice after saffron, because its flowers must be pollinated by hand; Madagascar grows most of the world's supply.

ja: 発酵食品は世界中にある。日本の味噌や納豆、韓国のキムチ、ドイツのザワークラウトなど、どの文化にも発酵の知恵がある。
easy: Many cultures have special foods made by small living things, like miso, kimchi and sauerkraut.
std: Fermented foods appear in cultures worldwide, from Japanese miso and natto to Korean kimchi and German sauerkraut.

ja: スポットライト効果：自分の失敗や見た目の変化に、他人は自分が思うほど気づいていない。
easy: Other people notice your mistakes much less than you think.
std: The spotlight effect: we overestimate how much other people notice our mistakes and appearance.

ja: 眠っている間に新しいことを覚えるのは難しい。でも昼に学んだことは、眠っている間に整理されて定着する。
easy: You cannot really learn new things while you sleep. But sleep helps you keep what you learned during the day.
std: Learning brand-new material during sleep is very limited, but sleep plays a key role in strengthening memories formed during the day.

ja: ドーパミンは「快楽の物質」というより、「ごほうびへの期待」や「やる気」にかかわる物質。
easy: Dopamine is more about wanting a reward than enjoying it.
std: Dopamine is linked less to pleasure itself than to anticipating rewards and motivating us to seek them.

ja: メラビアンの法則は「言葉より声や表情が大事」とよく紹介されるが、もとの研究は気持ちと言葉が食い違う場面に限った話。
easy: A famous study about body language is often used in the wrong way. It was only about feelings, not all talk.
std: Mehrabian's often-quoted '7-38-55' rule applies only to situations where words and tone conflict about feelings, not to all communication.

ja: 「成長マインドセット」：能力は努力で伸ばせると考える姿勢。ただし大規模な研究では、介入の効果は小さいという結果もある。
easy: Believing you can get better with work is called a growth mindset. Big studies show it helps only a little.
std: Carol Dweck's 'growth mindset' is the belief that abilities can be developed, though large studies suggest mindset programs have only small effects.

ja: 楽しいときは時間が早く、退屈なときや怖いときは遅く感じる。注意の向け方で時間の感じ方が変わるため。
easy: Time feels fast when you have fun and slow when you are bored or afraid.
std: Time seems to fly when we are enjoying ourselves and to drag when we are bored or frightened, because attention shapes our sense of time.

ja: 初期のコンピューターENIAC（1946年公開）は重さ30トン、真空管1万8000本で、部屋ひとつをうめつくした。
easy: ENIAC, an early computer from the 1940s, weighed 30 tons and filled a whole room.
std: ENIAC, unveiled in 1946, weighed about 30 tonnes, used some 18,000 vacuum tubes and filled an entire room.

ja: インターネットのもとになったARPANETの最初の通信（1969年）では、「LOGIN」と送ろうとして「LO」の2文字でシステムが止まった。
easy: The first message on the early internet in 1969 was meant to be 'LOGIN'. The system stopped after 'LO'.
std: The first message sent over ARPANET in 1969 was supposed to be 'LOGIN', but the system crashed after 'LO'.

ja: 「人工知能（AI）」ということばは、1956年のダートマス会議の提案書から広まった。
easy: The words 'artificial intelligence' became popular after a meeting in 1956.
std: The term 'artificial intelligence' was popularized by the 1956 Dartmouth workshop, often called the birth of AI as a field.

ja: 世界では数十億台のスマートフォンが使われている。初代iPhoneの発売（2007年）から20年足らずで急速に広まった。
easy: Billions of people now use smartphones. They spread very fast after 2007.
std: Billions of smartphones are in use today, most of them adopted in less than two decades after the first iPhone in 2007.

ja: 量子コンピューターが実用化されると、今の暗号の多くが破られるおそれがある。そのため「耐量子暗号」の標準づくりが進んでいる。
easy: Future quantum computers may break much of today's internet safety. People are making new kinds of codes to stop this.
std: Large quantum computers could break much of today's public-key encryption, so new 'post-quantum' standards are being developed.

ja: 遺伝子を狙って書きかえる技術CRISPR-Cas9は「遺伝子のはさみ」と呼ばれ、2020年にノーベル化学賞を受けた。
easy: CRISPR is a tool that can cut and change genes. Its makers won the Nobel Prize in 2020.
std: CRISPR-Cas9, nicknamed 'genetic scissors', earned its developers the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

ja: 「トロッコ問題」：1人を犠牲にして5人を助けるべきか、という思考実験。自動運転車の判断をめぐる議論でも取り上げられる。
easy: The trolley problem asks: should you hurt one person to save five? People talk about it when they make self-driving cars.
std: The trolley problem, whether to sacrifice one person to save five, is often discussed in debates about how self-driving cars should decide.

ja: サッカーは世界で最も人気のあるスポーツとされ、2022年W杯決勝は約15億人が見たと発表された。
easy: Football is the most popular sport in the world. About 1.5 billion people watched the 2022 World Cup final.
std: Football is widely seen as the world's most popular sport, and FIFA reported that about 1.5 billion people watched the 2022 World Cup final.
